errors.english: At the conclusion of the speech
errors.why: The praise of the king ('well done', Skt. nṛpasādhuvāde) was spreading to the ends of the directions; no speech is concluding.

errors.english: began to utter various expressions of disbelief
errors.why: The people broke into talk of baseless imaginings (abhūtārthavikalpajalpa), distraught speculation, not expressions of disbelief.

errors.english: With a body cut despite its great fragrance
errors.why: The mango tree's body is cut because of its fragrance (Skt. saurabhacchinnatanu), not in spite of it.
The verse is a gradation: the greedy give up kin, the pleasure-seeker gives up wealth, the compassionate give up even the body; the note misreads it.

note: Readable rendering of the lament verses, but the opening clause, the people's reaction and the mango-tree simile are skewed.

errors.english: gather extraordinary, non-common faults of the wise
errors.why: མཁས་པ here describes the misdeeds as 'skilled at bringing no small harm'; they are not 'faults of the wise'.

note: Faithful on the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son examples and the verses; one misparsed clause at the start.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
errors.why: ལྡན་པ is the Vaiśeṣika quality conjunction (saṃyoga): number and conjunction, both qualities, cannot belong to the categories.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
fix.replace: number and conjunction (saṃyoga) are also impossible for them, because both are qualities

errors.english: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
errors.why: The example is 'a row of mansions' (a collective expression like 'the group of six'), not a palace and a garland.

fix.find: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
fix.replace: it includes expressions such as "a row of mansions"

errors.english: Similarly, there is no differentiation among the collection of the six categories
errors.why: The sentence is a challenge: in expressions like 'the group of the six categories', if nothing distinct is there, how can one say 'six'? The English states a flat assertion instead.

errors.english: the essence of space cannot be differentiated from them
errors.why: The point is that the nature of space is not distinct from space itself, not that it cannot be differentiated from the qualities.

note: Follows the argument against the Vaiśeṣika categories broadly, but mistakes two technical examples and turns a rhetorical challenge into an assertion.

errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung, the standard example of a lotus arising from a heterogeneous cause.

errors.english: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', is an anthill, from which smoke-like vapour rises; that is the point of the verse.

fix.find: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
fix.replace: [note: śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', i.e. an anthill, from which smoke-like vapour rises]

errors.english: Otherwise, there would never be any purpose [note: original: "don"] at all.
errors.why: Here དོན is the entity and ལན་འགའ is 'occasional': otherwise the thing could not be occasional (kādācitka). It has nothing to do with a purpose.

note: The causal argument is mostly sound, but the stock examples (anthill, cow dung) and the occasionality argument are mistranslated.

errors.english: By the non-pacification of you and the cowherd
errors.why: Most likely 'by you and Śivā (Zhi ba), the cowherd's mother': Zhi ba is a proper name, the same person whose hand throws the curd-pot, not 'non-pacification'.
ཞོ་རྫིའུ is a small pot of curd, not a churner.
The Tibetan breaks off here (it continues 'is a dwelling' on the next side); 'unread syllable' is not in the text.

note: A word-gloss commentary rendered competently in most entries; one narrative gloss misreads a proper name and an object.
Both the Sanskrit and the Tibetan verses on Śuddhodana's funeral rites and the monks' question are rendered faithfully.

errors.english: possess an essence of diligence because the benefit of beings is never exhausted
errors.why: ཕན་མིན་ is what harms beings and ཟད་ཕྱིར་ means 'in order to end it': they strive by nature to end what harms beings.

fix.find: possess an essence of diligence because the benefit of beings is never exhausted
fix.replace: are by nature diligent in bringing to an end what harms beings

errors.english: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
errors.why: འབྱུང་བ here is the appearance (birth) of such beings; it is rare to meet the appearance of ones like you.

fix.find: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
fix.replace: the appearance of ones like yourselves is not easily found

errors.english: Until you have attained it, how could you remain so stable?
errors.why: The question is rhetorical: how could that state, grounded in your discipline, remain unattained by you? You will surely attain it.
The verse means that whoever has this understanding serves (relies on) the parents; it does not say the wisdom depends on them.

note: The prose frame and the jātaka opening are fine, but several of the verses are misparsed, one of them into the opposite sense.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on cetanā/cetayitvā karma, with root verses correctly set apart.
Faithful translation of the Akṣayamati quotation on right view and right intention and of the argument on abandoning latent tendencies.
Precise rendering of the discussion of contradictory reasons and the force of 'oneself' (svayam) in the definition of the thesis.
